# Implementation Plan: ralph-orchestration v5.49 spawn-and-ship UX bundle

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-03. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview

This plan bundles two complementary ralph-orchestration UX improvements that share the same review surface (`plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md`, `skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md`) and originate from real bookkeeper friction on the 2026-06 codexu workflow.

**US-001 (CODE):** Add a `--target-repo <path>` override flag to `/implement-with-ralph` so the lead/operator can force the target repo at spawn time. When provided, `convert-to-ralph-prd` Step 1 validates the path with `git -C <path> rev-parse --show-toplevel` and skips the ~30s plan-analysis Explore agent. When absent, behavior is unchanged.

**US-002 (DOCS-ONLY, Phase a only):** Add a generalized "Multi-repo wrapper-to-submodule ship ceremony" subsection to `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md` documenting the 7-step lead-owned ceremony (FF-merge → push to all submodule remotes → verify → bump wrapper pointer → update active-plugin-versions table → commit wrapper → `copilot plugin update`). Add a Phase 6 kind=done handoff prose block to `skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` that triggers when `prd.json.repoDir` is a submodule of the lead's wrapper. Cross-reference from codexu root `AGENTS.md`. Phase b (helper tooling) and Phase c (Phase 6 automation) are **explicitly deferred** to separate scopes.

**Branch mapping (per codexu AGENTS.md convention, distinct phases):**

| Phase | Branch | Worktree | Repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLAN (this work) | `ralph/plan-ralph-v5.49-bundle` | `.ralph/jobs/ralph-orchestration-spawn-target-repo-override-flag/worktree/plan/` | codexu |
| IMPL (next member) | `ralph/ralph-orchestration-spawn-target-repo-override-flag` | `ai-developer-toolkit/.worktrees/ralph-orchestration-spawn-target-repo-override-flag/` | ai-developer-toolkit submodule |

Both stories' code/docs land in the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule on the IMPL branch. Local commit + topic-branch push only; lead handles multi-remote push per codexu AGENTS.md's ask-before-pushing rule and the new US-002 ceremony itself.

- Markdown skill specs (canonical): `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.
- Copilot CLI mirrors: `.copilot-plugin/internal-workflows/<skill>/SKILL.md` (auto-generated by `scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --write`) and `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` (hand-forked, parity-checked by `scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs`).
- Node ESM helpers: `src/*.mjs`. Test runner: `node plugins/ralph/tests/run.mjs` (auto-discovers `test-*.mjs`).
- **No `package.json`** inside `plugins/ralph/` or `ai-developer-toolkit/`; tests are zero-dependency Node scripts plus bash smoke fixtures.
- Current pinned ralph version: **5.47.0** (`plugins/ralph/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugins/ralph/.github/plugin/plugin.json`, three marketplace indexes, and codexu's `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table). Per the US-001 prompt seed in `.ralph-overview/data.json`, this bundle targets **v5.49.0** (the operator's bundle name; v5.48 is reserved/skipped — surface as a confirmation note in the impl handoff).

### Technical Constraints

- **`convert-to-ralph-prd` Step 1** today runs an Explore agent using `prompts/repo-detector.md` to detect the target repo, then stores result as `target_repo` and writes it to `prd.json.repoDir` (Step 5 invocation; Step 8 PRD write). Batch flag list (lines 22-32) lacks `--target-repo`.
- **`worktree-create.mjs`** already accepts `--target-repo` (helpText lines 16-29; `requiredPath(opts.targetRepo, "--target-repo")` at line 60; parseArgs handles `case "--target-repo"`). Does NOT validate with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — assumes the path is valid.
- **`implement-with-ralph` Phase 1** today has no `--target-repo` flag. Existing flags: `--autonomous`, `--interactive`, `--batch`, `--codex-review`, `--copilot-review`, `--iteration-engine`, `--planning-engine`, `--job`, `--from-plan`, `--suggested-decomposition`, `--from-story`, `--pause-after`, `--skip`, `--parallel`, `--allow-stale-base`, `--edit-prd`, `--run-only`, `resume`.
- **Phase 6** of `implement-with-ralph` has an existing PR-creation handoff (v5.30.0 added for parallel-mode integration branch) BEFORE the terminal write. The new submodule-ship handoff follows the same pattern: lead-owned, completion-path-only, runs before `orchestrator.terminal = true`.
- **`prd.json.repoDir`** must be an absolute normalized path with forward slashes. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns the worktree root (acceptable — PRD wants the editable repo root, not the main repo's `.git` storage root).
- **Copilot artifact parity is a release gate.** Before shipping, the impl member MUST run `node plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --check && node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` from the toolkit submodule root.
- **CI invariant.** Codexu's `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table for `ralph` MUST be bumped in the same commit as the submodule pointer-bump that lands the new plugin version. This is itself an instance of the US-002 ceremony.

## Approach

### Architecture

**US-001 data flow.** The flag flows: `/implement-with-ralph --target-repo <path>` → Phase 1 arg parse → Phase 2 forwards to `convert-to-ralph-prd --target-repo <path>` → Step 1 validates and short-circuits the Explore agent → Step 5 unchanged consumer of `target_repo` → Step 8 writes `repoDir`. Validation lives in BOTH layers: eager parse-time in `implement-with-ralph` Phase 1 (fail fast) AND hard validation in `convert-to-ralph-prd` Step 1 (defends direct skill invocations that bypass the parent).

**US-002 generalization rule.** Single source of truth = `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md`. Codexu's `AGENTS.md` Bookkeeper Operating Invariants section gets ONE backlink line pointing at the canonical version. Use noun placeholders (`<wrapper-repo>`, `<submodule>`, `<submodule-remotes>`, `<submodule-main>`, `<wrapper-main>`, `<consumer-machine>`) in the ralph-side prose so other wrapper repos can adapt without editing the canonical text.

**Phase 6 trigger detection — wrapper-root-aware (F-001 fix).** A naive `git -C <repo_root> submodule status` FAILS because `repo_root` in Phase 6 is the TARGET repo (= `prd.json.repoDir`), which IS the submodule when this trigger should fire. The check must run inside the WRAPPER repo, not the submodule. Derive the wrapper root from `<job_dir>` (standalone: `wrapper_root = "$(realpath "$job_dir/../../..")"` since `job_dir = <wrapper>/.ralph/jobs/<name>/`) or `<group_dir>` (group: `wrapper_root = "$(realpath "$group_dir/../../..")"`). Validate the derivation: `git -C "$wrapper_root" rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1`. Then compute `relative_repoDir = $(realpath --relative-to="$wrapper_root" "$repoDir")` and run `git -C "$wrapper_root" submodule status -- "$relative_repoDir"`. Non-empty stdout + exit 0 → IS a submodule of the wrapper → emit handoff prose. Empty stdout / non-zero exit → not a submodule → skip the handoff. The check is cheap (two git commands, no network).

### Implementation Strategy

1. **US-001 first (serial dependency on shared files).** Land flag + validation + tests + parity refresh. This is the CODE story.
2. **US-002 second.** Add the generalized ceremony subsection + Phase 6 handoff prose + codexu backlink. This is the DOCS story; it inherits any Phase 6 / Phase 1 structural changes US-001 made (which is why they must be serial — both touch `skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md`).

### Out of Scope

- **Phase b** (helper tooling — `pnpm ralph:ship-submodule <task-id>` automation script). DEFERRED to a separate `ralph-orchestration-ship-submodule-helper` task. The docs alone (Phase a) are valuable even without tooling because the lead is the human who decides when to ship.
- **Phase c** (Phase 6 auto-run of the ceremony). DEFERRED — that's a bigger UX shift involving cross-repo write permissions and multi-remote auth that needs its own design pass. Phase 6 in this scope only MENTIONS the ceremony in the kind=done report.
- Changes to `worktree-create.mjs`'s actual `--target-repo` resolution logic (it already works correctly).
- Changes to the `prompts/repo-detector.md` Explore-agent prompt (still used by the fallback path).
- Changes to other ralph skills (`brainstorm-with-ralph`, `plan-with-ralph`, `decompose-plan`, `parallel-ralph`).
- Schema changes to `prd.json.repoDir` (still string; still required).
- Adding a `--target-repo` PRD field (the flag is a spawn-time override only; persistence happens through the existing `prd.json.repoDir` write in Step 8).
- Codexu data.json bookkeeping updates beyond the AGENTS.md backlink line.

## Risk Areas

1. **Plan-analysis side-effect loss.** Skipping the Explore agent loses: (a) plan-file/research-brief scan, (b) interactive confirmation branch, (c) notepad log side effect (SKILL.md lines 277-283 per architect). There is NO scope/cluster analysis lost — those are out of scope for Step 1 today. Mitigation: document the trade-off explicitly in `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md`; the operator opts in by passing the flag, so the loss is by design.

2. **Copilot mirror drift.** Two mirrors must stay in sync: `.copilot-plugin/internal-workflows/convert-to-ralph-prd/SKILL.md` is GENERATED (run `generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --write`), while `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` is HAND-FORKED (must be edited by hand with matching `<!-- src: ... -->` anchors). Forgetting the hand-mirror produces a parity-check failure that blocks the release gate. Mitigation: impl prompt MUST run BOTH `generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --check` AND `check-copilot-parity.mjs` before commit.

3. **Phase 6 trigger detection false positives.** If `prd.json.repoDir == repo_root` (impl in the wrapper directly), the new handoff prose MUST NOT fire. The `git submodule status -- <relative_path>` check returns non-empty only for genuine submodule paths, so this is naturally guarded. Mitigation: explicitly test the trigger in the impl with a fixture where `repoDir == repo_root` → handoff prose NOT emitted; with `repoDir` inside `ai-developer-toolkit/` → handoff prose emitted.

4. **Doc drift between codexu and ralph AGENTS.md.** If both files describe the ceremony in different prose, they will drift. Mitigation: the rule is "ralph AGENTS.md is the canonical source; codexu's AGENTS.md backlinks ONLY." The backlink line MUST say this explicitly so future editors of codexu don't elaborate the ceremony in place.

5. **Version skip 5.48 → 5.49.** The operator's bundle name says "v5.49" but current version is 5.47.0, skipping 5.48. The data.json mentions "5.48" in 3 places (likely cross-references from other in-flight or shipped tasks; not blocking). Mitigation: impl member should surface this as a kind=question on first turn IF the skip feels wrong (e.g., if a sibling v5.48 ship lands first). Otherwise, proceed with 5.49.0 per the explicit operator brief.

6. **Test infrastructure is markdown-contract style.** Because `convert-to-ralph-prd` is a Markdown workflow not an executable CLI, the new tests assert SKILL.md prose contains the override branch, validation command, etc. They are NOT executable end-to-end tests. Mitigation: the test design is explicitly contract-style; documented as such in the test file's leading comment. End-to-end behavior is exercised by the existing `tests/test-submodule-worktree-init.sh` fixture pattern (bash + git) — if impl scope expands later, that's the template.

7. **Workspace contamination in the plan worktree.** The plan worktree at `.ralph/jobs/ralph-orchestration-spawn-target-repo-override-flag/worktree/plan/` has the `ai-developer-toolkit/` submodule initialized as part of the codexu checkout. Impl members must use the SUBMODULE worktree convention (per codexu AGENTS.md): `git -C ai-developer-toolkit worktree add ai-developer-toolkit/.worktrees/ralph-orchestration-spawn-target-repo-override-flag -b ralph/<task-id> main` and commit inside that submodule worktree, NOT in the plan worktree directly. Mitigation: impl prompt MUST hard-code this — it's not the plan-worktree's role to be edited by the impl.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

### US-001: --target-repo override flag for /implement-with-ralph

**Description:** As a bookkeeper-lead, I want a `--target-repo <path>` spawn-time override flag on `/implement-with-ralph` so I can force the target repo when (a) the plan touches both wrapper + submodule files and the plan-analysis agent picks wrong, (b) a submodule-only task where the agent would fall back to cwd, or (c) I want to fix an issue in a sibling repo not declared in any prd.json — without paying the ~30s plan-analysis cost.

**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-001 through AC-010 (above).
**Dependencies:** None.
**Estimated complexity:** medium.

### US-002: Multi-repo wrapper-to-submodule ship ceremony docs

**Description:** As a bookkeeper-lead, I want the 7-step submodule-ship ceremony documented in `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md` with repo-agnostic placeholders, plus a Phase 6 kind=done handoff prose block in `implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` that triggers when `prd.json.repoDir` is a submodule of my wrapper, so I and any future bookkeeper on a different wrapper repo don't have to re-derive the ceremony from scratch each ship.

**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-011 through AC-015 (above).
**Dependencies:** US-001 (shared file overlap on `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md` and `plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md`).
**Estimated complexity:** small (docs-only; no code, no tests).

### Bundle-level shared deliverables

- AC-016: Version bumps across 6 files (5 toolkit + 1 codexu).
- AC-017: CHANGELOG.md v5.49.0 entry.
- AC-018: Phase 5a + 5b review convergence.
- AC-019: bash test-submodule-worktree-init.sh passes (F-003).
- AC-020: --parallel + --target-repo rejection (F-004).

## Appendix C: Ceremony prose template (US-002 reference)

The impl member writes the following prose (with placeholders) into `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md`. Exact wording can be refined during Phase 5b docs review:

```markdown
## Multi-repo wrapper-to-submodule ship ceremony

When `ralph-orchestration` runs against a `<wrapper-repo>` that hosts plugins
inside a `<submodule>`, shipping an impl that lands edits in the submodule
requires a 7-step lead-owned ceremony. The impl member commits inside the
submodule worktree; the lead handles steps 1-7 below.

1. **FF-merge the submodule topic branch to `<submodule>/<submodule-main>`.**
   `git -C <submodule> merge --ff-only <topic-branch>`

2. **Push `<submodule-main>` to all `<submodule-remotes>` in lockstep.**
   `git -C <submodule> remote | xargs -I {} git -C <submodule> push {} <submodule-main>`
   Stale remotes cause `copilot plugin update` and equivalent commands to
   silently leave consumer machines on the old plugin version. Every remote
   MUST advance in the same operator session.

3. **Verify each `<submodule-remotes>` `<submodule-main>` HEAD matches local.**
   `git -C <submodule> ls-remote --heads <remote-name> <submodule-main>`
   Compare against `git -C <submodule> rev-parse <submodule-main>` on local.

4. **Bump the `<wrapper-repo>` submodule pointer.**
   `git -C <wrapper-repo> add <submodule>`

5. **Update the `<wrapper-repo>` active-plugin-versions table.**
   If the submodule edit changed a plugin manifest version, update
   `<wrapper-repo>/AGENTS.md` (or the wrapper's equivalent CI-invariant doc)
   in the SAME commit as the pointer bump. Stale tables trip CI invariants
   and leave consumers querying the wrong version.

6. **Commit the wrapper pointer + table edit + push wrapper remotes.**
   `git -C <wrapper-repo> commit -m "chore: bump <submodule> for <feature>"`
   `git -C <wrapper-repo> remote | xargs -I {} git -C <wrapper-repo> push {} <wrapper-main>`

7. **Refresh consumer machines.**
   Each `<consumer-machine>` runs the equivalent of
   `copilot plugin update --all` (or the wrapper's equivalent) to pull the
   bumped plugin version. This step depends on step 2 — if any
   `<submodule-remotes>` is stale, consumers stay on the old version even
   after running the update command.

This ceremony is documented HERE as the canonical version. Wrapper-repo
maintainers (e.g. codexu, other forks) should backlink to this section
from their own AGENTS.md rather than duplicating the prose in place.
```

## Appendix D: Phase 6 prose template (US-002 reference; F-001 + F-009 fixes applied)

The impl member adds this block to `plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` Phase 6, BEFORE the terminal write (before `orchestrator.terminal = true` and before `<ralph-orchestrator>COMPLETE</ralph-orchestrator>`):

```markdown
### Lead handoff for submodule ship (Phase 6, before terminal write)

When `prd.json.repoDir` is a submodule of the lead's WRAPPER repo (NOT the
target repo, which IS the submodule when this trigger fires), the impl
cannot ship the work end-to-end on its own — the lead must run the 7-step
ceremony documented at `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md` "Multi-repo wrapper-to-
submodule ship ceremony". Surface this handoff in the Phase 6 terminal
output AND in `<job_dir>/progress.txt` so the lead is reminded.

Detection (derive WRAPPER root from job_dir / group_dir — NOT from repo_root
which is the target repo / submodule itself):

```bash
# Standalone job: job_dir is <wrapper>/.ralph/jobs/<name>/
# Group job: group_dir is <wrapper>/.ralph/job-groups/<name>/ — adapt the realpath
if [ -n "$group_dir" ]; then
  wrapper_root=$(realpath "$group_dir/../../..")
else
  wrapper_root=$(realpath "$job_dir/../../..")
fi

# Sanity-check the derived wrapper is a git repo
if ! git -C "$wrapper_root" rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  IS_SUBMODULE=false
else
  relative_repoDir=$(realpath --relative-to="$wrapper_root" "$repoDir")
  if status=$(git -C "$wrapper_root" submodule status -- "$relative_repoDir" 2>/dev/null) && \
     [ -n "$status" ]; then
    IS_SUBMODULE=true
  else
    IS_SUBMODULE=false
  fi
fi
```

When `IS_SUBMODULE=true`:

1. **Echo the handoff prose to stdout** (BEFORE the `<ralph-orchestrator>COMPLETE</ralph-orchestrator>`
   marker), tailoring `<submodule>` / `<topic-branch>` / `<wrapper-main>` /
   `<submodule-main>` to the actual paths derived above.

2. **Append to `<job_dir>/progress.txt`** under a new section:
   ```
   ## Orchestrator Notes
   ### Submodule ship handoff (lead-owned, $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))
   <same prose as the stdout echo>
   ```

Sample tailored prose (echoed + appended):

> **Submodule ship handoff (lead-owned).** This impl committed inside
> `<submodule>` on topic branch `<topic-branch>`. To ship end-to-end:
> 1. FF-merge in `<submodule>` to `<submodule-main>`, 2. push to all
> `<submodule-remotes>`, 3. verify remote heads, 4. bump wrapper pointer in
> `<wrapper_root>`, 5. update active-plugin-versions table (if changed),
> 6. commit + push wrapper to all `<wrapper-remotes>`, 7. refresh consumer
> machines. See `<wrapper_root>/<plugin-root>/AGENTS.md` "Multi-repo
> wrapper-to-submodule ship ceremony" for full commands.

This runs BEFORE the terminal write so that if the handoff prose emission
crashes, the next Phase 6 entry re-runs it (matches the v5.30.0
PR-creation handoff pattern, which also runs before terminal write).

NOTE: This is plain stdout output + progress.txt append — NOT a crews
mailbox `kind=done` envelope. The impl-member's crews wrapper (if any)
will surface the prose to the operator via its own kind=done emission;
that's outside the SKILL.md contract. The SKILL.md only writes to the
two destinations above.
```
